text: There was a famine in the land, besides the earlier famine that had come in the days of Abraham, and Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
The LORD appeared to him and said: "Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land I will tell you of.

versions.text: The LORD appeared to him and said: "Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land I will show you.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is אֹמַר ("I will say/tell"), not רָאָה ("show"). The distinction echoes the wording of Abraham's call and should be preserved.

text: Live in this land as a stranger, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will fulfill the oath I swore to Abraham your father.
I will make your offspring as many as the stars of heaven, and I will give your offspring all these lands, and through your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed—
because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws."
So Isaac stayed in Gerar.
When the men of the place asked about his wife, he said, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say "my wife," thinking, "The men of the place might kill me over Rebekah, because she is beautiful."
After he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down through a window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah his wife.
Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, "So she is your wife! How could you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac answered him, "Because I thought I might die on account of her."
Abimelech said, "What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us."
So Abimelech gave orders to all the people: "Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death."
Isaac sowed in that land, and that same year he reaped a hundredfold, for the LORD blessed him.
The man grew rich, and he kept growing richer until he became very wealthy.
He had flocks and herds and a large household, and the Philistines envied him.
All the wells his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father the Philistines had stopped up and filled with earth.
Then Abimelech said to Isaac, "Move away from us, for you have become far too powerful for us."
So Isaac left there, camped in the Valley of Gerar, and settled there.

Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham's death, and he gave them the same names his father had given them.
Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of fresh water.
But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, "The water is ours!" So he named the well Esek, because they contended with him. [Footnote: Esek means "contention."]

versions.text: But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, "The water is ours!" So he named the well Esek, because they contended with him.
versions.explanation: The wordplay between the name and the reason for it is lost for hearers; a brief footnote giving the meaning of the name preserves the sense without cluttering the read-aloud text.

text: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too; so he named it Sitnah.
He moved on from there and dug another well, and over that one they did not quarrel. He named it Rehoboth, saying, "Now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land."
From there he went up to Beersheba.

That night the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham my servant."
So he built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD. He pitched his tent there, and there Isaac's servants dug a well.
Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me, since you hated me and sent me away from you?"
They answered, "We have seen clearly that the LORD has been with you, so we said: Let there be a sworn agreement between us—between us and you—and let us make a covenant with you,
that you will do us no harm, just as we did not touch you but did you nothing but good and sent you away in peace. You are now blessed by the LORD."
So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
Early in the morning they rose and exchanged oaths with one another. Then Isaac sent them off, and they left him in peace.
That same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug, and said to him, "We have found water!"

He named it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day. [Footnote: Shibah sounds like the Hebrew words for "oath" and "seven"; Beersheba means "well of the oath" or "well of seven."]

versions.text: He named it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
versions.explanation: Without a note, the connection between the well's name and the city's name is opaque to English hearers.

text: When Esau was forty years old, he married Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
They were a bitter grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
